headline: Approved rideshare pickup and drop-off locations for the October 2026 season, including the Margin Street and Dodge Street lots.
summary: Commissioners agreed Salem should have truck safety rules similar to Boston, Somerville, and Cambridge, and staff will seek feedback from city departments before drafting an ordinance. The commission also approved an order designating the proposed locations as rideshare pickup spots for the October 2026 season. Members approved the June 24, 2026 minutes.

plain_text:
City of Salem 
Transportation Commission 
Meeting Minutes 
Wednesday August 12, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Transportation Commission was held remotely on Wednesday, 
August 12, 2026, at 6:00pm, in accordance with Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025. 
 
Present: Chair Jaime Garmendia, Vice Chair Jeff Swartz, Commissioner Brendan Casey, 
Commissioner Emmylou Manwill, and Commissioner Michael Egan. Also present were 
Transportation Director David Kucharsky, Transportation Data Analyst Russell Findley, 
Transportation Planner Eric Gemperline, and Transportation Commission advisory 
members. Absent: None 
 
CALL OF MEETING 
 
The meeting was called to order at 6:00pm by Chair Garmendia. He explains how members 
of the public may participate during the remote meeting. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENTS 
 
Chair Garmendia opens the floor to public comment. 
 
Brendan (no last name or address provided) expresses concerns regarding resident permit 
parking. He suggests having to input information for visiting cars is cumbersome and 
beyond some people’s ability, and that the information being requested is unnecessary and 
potentially perilous. He expresses concerns regarding data sharing and suggests a better 
system would be a sticker or placard situation to identify license plates that should be 
allowed to park in a particular zone. 
 
Ward 1 City Councilor Erin Turowski introduces herself and states she is in favor of both of 
the proposals being discussed this evening, noting that she is unsure if she will be able to 
stay the whole meeting. She also thanks staff for installing a new speed radar on Derby 
Street. 
 
Commissioners Garmendia and Manwill speak to the recent No Turn On Red sign 
installations and their good visibility. 
 
Mr. Kucharsky notes that for visitor passes the only information being requested is the 
plate number. He also notes that anyone having difficulty with the parking app can come 
into City Hall and receive assistance or call during business hours.
NEW/OLD BUSINESS 
 
Director’s Update 
 
Mr. Kucharsky provides updates regarding the ped-activated No Right Turn on Red signs 
installed throughout the City, and he notes that static signs are also being installed in 
multiple locations. Mr. Kucharsky notes sidewalk work on Salem Street as well as drainage 
work. Mr. Kucharsky also discusses installation of permanent speed humps at Gardner, 
Palmer, Leavitt, Dow, and Harbor Streets. Mr. Kucharsky indicates that the Brown Street 
tactical pilot upgrades are only partially complete, noting that additional water main valves 
need to be replaced in the intersection prior to installation of final elements such as flex 
posts. He also notes progress regarding the Congress Street and Boardman Street 
crosswalks, including work for drainage and resetting sidewalks. Mr. Kucharsky discusses 
preparations for October season including signage. 
 
Commissioner Manwill thanks staff for updating the website with information regarding 
the Salem Skipper and asks if there are plans to incorporate an updated paving map into 
the GIS system. Mr. Kucharsky indicates that engineering works on that but that he will 
pass the message along. 
 
Truck Safety Ordinances 
 
Chair Garmendia explains that this agenda item relates to a recent incident where a City of 
Boston transportation planner was recently killed in crash where a commercial truck hit 
her while she was traveling by bicycle. He indicates the truck went to move around a 
stopped car and veered into the bike lane coming into collision with the individual.  
 
Mr. Kucharsky and Mr. Gemperline review examples of truck and commercial vehicle 
ordinances that have been passed at the state and local level with the goal of proposing 
ordinance amendments for the City Council to consider and adopt. 
 
Mr. Gemperline provides a truck safety overview, discussing truck lateral protective 
devices which are designed to keep pedestrians, bicyclists, and motorcyclists from being 
run over by a large truck’s rear wheels in a side impact collision. He also notes that the 
deadliest road crashes are those between large trucks and pedestrians or cyclists. Mr. 
Gemperline explains that in 2015 Boston passed the nation’s first truck side guard 
ordinance, which requires that enhanced safety measures be installed on all city-owned 
and city-contracted motor vehicles weighing over 10,000 pounds, and semi-trailers 
exceeding 26,000 pounds. Somerville and Cambridge adopted similar ordinances in 2017 
and 2020, respectively. In 2022 the Act to Reduce Traffic Fatalities (Chapter 358 of the Acts 
of 2022 amended M.G.L. c. 90, section 7) was introduced. Staff notes that Salem currently 
has no truck-related safety ordinances. Additional details and requirements regarding the 
truck side-guard ordinances of Boston, Somerville, and Cambridge are discussed, as well as 
the specifics of the 2022 Act to Reduce Traffic Fatalities, which created the legal framework 
for improving truck safety and protecting vulnerable road users, and updates/amendments 
to date. As of July 1, 2025, snow and ice removal contracts through MassDOT are subject to
the truck safety devices program, which requires backup cameras, side underside guards, 
convex mirrors, and crossover mirrors. 
 
Mr. Gemperline next discusses challenges with respect to enforcement in each of the cities, 
and notes that enforcement efforts include utilizing traffic enforcement officers to monitor 
and levy penalties, as well as police department enforcement. MassDOT requires all 
contractors to register with the RMV and provide a sticker. Mr. Gemperline next discusses 
Amendment 160 - Protecting Vulnerable Road Users, which was part of the 2026 Economic 
Development Bill (S.3178) and adopted by the Senate on July 26, 2026. The amendment 
creates a presumption of negligence when a Class 3 or larger truck is involved in a crash 
with a vulnerable road user, such as a pedestrian or bicyclist, unless the truck is equipped 
with the key safety technologies, including lateral protective devices, mirror, and back up 
cameras that meet MassDOT standards.  
 
Proposed next steps for the City of Salem are to get feedback from Salem Police, Fire, DPS, 
Finance, and the Mayor’s office, and then begin drafting an ordinance for Salem. 
Commissioners discuss the matter and agree that the City of Salem should have similar 
ordinances with similar safety criteria. They also discuss potential options for enforcement, 
as well as potential issues of costs for smaller businesses related to snow removal. Staff and 
commissioners continue to discuss.  
 
Chair Garmendia opens the floor to public comment but there is none. 
 
Taxi & Ridesharing October Pick-up/Drop-off Locations 
 
Mr. Gemperline presents a map showing rideshare and taxicab stand locations in Salem as 
they currently exist according to City ordinances. He notes that there is currently no 
signage delineating taxicab stands and reviews the existing ordinance language. The 
ordinance states that no person shall park a vehicle other than a taxicab upon any street 
within a business district in any taxicab stand, and that no person shall park a taxicab upon 
any street within a business district at any place other than the taxicab stand or stands 
designated for the use of their taxicab or taxicabs, except while engaged or while waiting 
for an opportunity to use a taxicab stand designated for their use. Staff recommend that the 
existing ordinances be rescinded, and new language be drafted. They also propose the 
following locations for taxi and rideshare pickup and drop-off locations in October: North 
Street at the Franklin Street lot; the Green Trail at North Street and Leslie’s retreat; Margin 
Street near Lifebridge; the old Salem jail lot, and Dodge Street. 
 
Commissioners discuss and provide feedback on the proposed locations. Staff answer 
clarifying questions. Commissioner Swartz suggests the Green Trail location should be on 
the opposite side and also expresses concerns regarding October density and the Margin 
Street location. He suggests additional potential locations on Lafayette Street and Derby 
Street that may be better alternatives. He also suggests one in the Bridge Street Neck area 
would be helpful as well. Mr. Swartz asks if this would be month-long or just weekends in
October.  Mr. Kucharsky indicates it would be weekends only most likely. He also says that 
the City has had discussions with Lyft and Uber, and in addition to being notified when 
there is a road closure, they are open to adding notifications into their algorithm to notify 
drivers if there is an easy access area in and out of the City to pick someone up. 
Commissioner Manwill suggests trying to force rideshare drivers to utilize the pickup and 
drop-off locations in October to help with congestions issues. She also agrees with the 
concern regarding the Margin Street lot location and suggests no idling if possible. 
Commissioner Egan suggests exceptions for people with disabilities and mobility issues 
that are using a rideshare service in terms of location, and the Commissioners discuss. Lt. 
Tucker speaks about the road closures that already occur during October with heavy 
pedestrian volumes, so people are already being forced to the outside edges of the 
downtown during these times. The Commissioners and staff continue to discuss the 
locations and logistics. Mr. Kucharsky also discusses the shuttle bus service from prior 
years and explains why the service was not able to be procured and established for this 
October. There will be free parking at the 108 Jefferson Avenue lot during October 
weekends. Mr. Kucharsky also notes that staff are looking for additional funds to see if they 
can continue to offer the Skipper service. 
 
Commissioners discuss whether an ordinance change or an order to pilot the locations 
would make more sense and determine an order may be appropriate. 
 
Chair Garmendia opens the floor to public comment but there is none. 
 
Motion and Vote: Commissioner Swartz motions to approve an order designating the 
suggested locations as rideshare pickup locations for the October 2026 season. 
Commissioner Egan seconds the motion. The vote is five (5) in favor, and none (0) 
opposed, the motion passes. 
 
OTHER BUSINESS THAT MAY LEGALLY COME BEFORE THE COMMISSION 
 
None 
 
UPCOMING MEETINGS SCHEDULE 
 
The next meeting is scheduled for September 9, 2026, at 6:00PM.  
 
MEETING MINUTES APPROVAL 
 
June 24, 2026 
 
Motion and Vote: Commissioner Swartz motions to approve the minutes for the June 24, 
2026, meeting of the Transportation Commission. Commissioner Casey seconds the 
motion. The vote is five (5) in favor, and none (0) opposed, the motion passes.
ADJOURNMENT 
 
On a motion duly made by Commissioner Swartz and seconded by Commissioner Egan the 
Transportation Commission meeting was adjourned at 7:49 PM.
